# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [today's date]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-11 — Reference number POC-8E43F25837-44913**
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Governing policy:** *Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery — Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026* (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf)

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) requested for me by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD. Cigna's notice dated August 11, 2026 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity. The notice does not identify which document or which criterion was missing.

I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision. Below, I have set out the plan's own criteria from the policy named above, exactly as they are written, and matched each one to what is already in my medical records. I am also asking Cigna to tell me specifically what it found missing, so that anything genuinely absent can be supplied rather than left to guesswork.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Symptoms**

The policy requires:

> "Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and that significantly limits activities"

My records document 24 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. They describe sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat. That is groin-dominant pain, worsened by flexion, significantly limiting my activities.

**2. Imaging**

The policy requires:

> "Imaging shows BOTH of the following findings:"

and

> "femoroacetabular impingement confirmed on x-ray, MRI, or CT with ANY of the following findings:"

with the listed options including:

> "presence of Tönnis Grade 0-1 osteoarthritis"

> "decrease of femoral head-neck offset"

> "acetabular retroversion (i.e., crossover sign, ischial spine sign)"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip, dated June 8, 2026, shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees, with joint space preserved and Tönnis grade 0. That report confirms femoroacetabular impingement on MRI and documents Tönnis Grade 0 osteoarthritis — which is one of the findings the policy itself lists. The imaging study is dated and in the file; if it was not attached to the request Cigna reviewed, I ask that it be obtained from Dr. Okafor's office and reviewed before a decision is made.

**3. Physical examination**

The policy requires:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings:"

> "positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation)"

> "limited passive hip internal rotation"

My records state that examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. If Cigna needs the examination described in the specific wording used in its policy, the complete office examination note from Dr. Okafor dated [date of examination note] can be submitted. I would ask that this be requested rather than treated as an absence of findings, since an examination was performed and documented.

**4. Non-surgical management**

The policy requires:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

and includes:

> "an image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within two (2) weeks after the injection)"

My records document:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, with activity modification, from May 26, 2026 through July 21, 2026 — 8 weeks, 18 visits completed, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 23, 2026, which gave three weeks of partial relief.

Taken together, my provider-directed non-surgical care spans more than three months, and the injection produced a documented positive response — partial pain relief. If Cigna requires confirmation that the injection was image-guided, the injection procedure note from [name of facility or provider who performed the injection] can be supplied on request.

## A note about the policy language

Several of the excerpts above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I am not able to address criteria I have not been shown. If Cigna's decision rests on any requirement in *Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery — Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026* other than those quoted above, I ask that the plan identify that requirement in writing so I can respond to it directly.

I would also note that the denial states only that documentation was incomplete. Under a denial for incomplete documentation, I am asking Cigna to list the specific records it considers missing. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the imaging, therapy, medication and injection records described above already exist and can be provided promptly.

## Closing request

I respectfully ask Cigna to overturn the denial dated August 11, 2026 (reference POC-8E43F25837-44913) and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914, as requested by Dr. Okafor. In the alternative, I ask that Cigna identify in writing the exact documentation it requires and the specific policy criterion it found unmet, and hold the appeal open so those records can be submitted.

I understand my appeal must be received by February 7, 2027, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal through my plan's appeal process — online at my.cigna.com, by phone at 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my card, and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which is the address I am using for this submission.

Please send all correspondence about this appeal to me at the address above, with a copy to Dr. Okafor. I authorize Cigna to discuss this appeal with Dr. Okafor's office.

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

**Casey Hayes**
Member ID: W225149976
Reference: POC-8E43F25837-44913
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-08], [physical therapy discharge note], [office examination note from Dr. Okafor], [injection procedure note dated 2026-05-23], [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-11]
